root_cause.text: The retry logic in shmem_undo_range for a failed shmem_free_swap on a large swap entry did not round down the truncation index to the entry's base index, allowing the same entry to be found repeatedly when the truncate index falls in the middle of a large swap entry that does not cross the end boundary, causing an infinite loop.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states: "When `index` points to the middle of a large swap entry, and the large swap entry doesn't go across the end border, find_get_entries() will return that large swap entry ... shmem_free_swap() will fail ... retry with the same index. The next iteration will find the same entry again ... leading to an infinite loop." The fix changes the retry to `index = base;` where `base = round_down(indices[i], 1 << order)`, ensuring the index is aligned to the swap entry's base.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix handling of large swap entries that cross the start of the truncation range in shmem_undo_range by aligning the index and checking both start and end boundaries.
intent_record.what: Added a local variable 'base' initialized to indices[i], moved and expanded the comment to mention both end and start borders, changed the conditional to first check order > 0, then round_down base to the large swap order, and skip if base < start or base + (1<<order) > end. Also changed the retry assignment from index = indices[i] to index = base.
intent_record.how: This ensures that large swap entries that cross either the start or end of the truncation range are skipped, while entries fully contained within the range are retried at their properly aligned base index. Previously only the end crossing was handled; now the start crossing is also handled.

grouping_result.intent: Fix handling of large swap entries that cross the start of the truncation range in shmem_undo_range by aligning the index and checking both start and end boundaries.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by fixing the handling of large swap entries that cross the truncation start boundary, aligning the index to the entry's base index, and checking boundaries to prevent the infinite loop caused by the retry logic.

candidates.rationale: When shmem_free_swap fails (returns 0) for a large swap entry that does not cross the end boundary, the code sets index = indices[i] without rounding down to the base index of the large swap entry. This causes the retry loop to start from the same index, allowing the same entry to be found repeatedly, leading to an infinite loop.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement sets the truncation index to the unadjusted value from indices[i], without rounding down to the base index of a large swap entry. When shmem_free_swap fails on a large swap entry that does not cross the end boundary, the retry loop starts from the same index, causing the same entry to be found repeatedly and resulting in an infinite loop.
